answer: At a coastal haven, a reef restoration fund auctions a fixed number of pigment-tracer survey slots, each tied to a different tide window. To claim a slot, an agent posts a bond and later supplies a sealed water sample that an independent lab checks. A sample identifier pays only once, so aliases cannot multiply one survey into many rewards. To run ten identities, an attacker must finance ten bonds, win ten slots, collect ten distinct samples and risk forfeiture for fakes. Wealth can still buy many slots and labs can collude, so cap concentration and rotate audited labs.
